The bare-token warning in why and avoid retains the distinction between lexical discovery and proof.
Why explicitly says a bare token passes discovery while proving nothing.
Then requires the behavioral proof and avoid rejects token-only remediation.
Claim heading is replaced by the corresponding read-and-identify preparation in prefer[0]; no substantive instruction is removed.

activation.note: Activation retains the Bun route-space and e2e scope, excludes route-free YAML and other stacks, and distinguishes lexical findings from semantic proof review. Change and deletion scenarios are declared additions derived from the continuing coverage obligation; behavioral adequacy is honestly labeled llm_judged rather than token-observable. The fires examples supplement the general given/when rather than replacing its scope.

audit.summary: All 62 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with structural headings compressed into corresponding instruction groups. The rewrite retains the distinction between detector coverage and meaningful production-path proof, preserves the authored exceptions, and keeps rule-specific blocking details local while sharing only generic strict-disposition policy.

segmentChecks.note: The route-space glob is in activation, while given/when/then and avoid preserve the coverage obligation, production InterlockingRunner-to-TrainRunner path, and prohibition on descriptive-only assertions. Provenance remains in audit/verifier_detail.
The warning against a merely mentioned route/train survives as the bare-token warning in why and avoid[0].
Why explicitly distinguishes passing lexical discovery from proving behavior; no substantive knowledge is lost.
Then requires a behavioral production-path proof and avoid[0] rejects a token-only fix, together preserving the remediation instruction.
The Claim heading is structural; prefer[0] retains both preparation steps associated with it.
The Stimulus heading is structural, with placement, resolution, and execution instructions retained in prefer and then.
The Witness heading is replaced by the actual selection assertion in then and conditional execution-outcome assertion in prefer[3].
The Verify heading is structurally rendered by the evidence checklist, which retains all three verification checks.
The shared node safely generalizes strict blocking, while why and verifier_detail[6] locally preserve the precise uncovered-admissible-route blocking condition.
Strict disposition is present in the shared policy and repeated locally with its rule-specific consequence; the generic sharing does not broaden the rule.
Verifier_detail preserves parsing, extracted route fields, routeId/trainId scanning, the e2e glob, and comment masking.
Verifier_detail[2] and evidence[0] preserve the at-least-one-test lexical coverage criterion and both accepted identifiers.
Verifier_detail[2] explicitly calls the token a discovery proxy rather than the objective, reinforced by avoid and unless.
Prefer[0] retains the requirement to choose guard-true inputs that distinguish the route from alternatives.
Unless, activation, and verifier_detail preserve the no-routes exception and both registry-index/generated-projection examples.
Verifier_detail[7] preserves the complete admissible_route definition, including routeId, resolved trainId, category, guard_ref, and authoritative source reference.

risks: The coder-facing fields do not give the authoritative source glob plan/_trains/_interlockings/**/*.yaml; a weak tester may have to guess where to discover all declared routes.

Comment masking is absent from the coder-facing fields. Although token-only remediation is discouraged, unless[1] broadly says any routeId/trainId reference is not flagged, which could mislead a weak tester about comment-only references.

The lexical exception ('not flagged') and semantic obligation ('token-only test still fails review') require careful reading; the rewrite does not explicitly instruct the tester to repair an existing token-only test.

unobservable: change: needs_new_observer; diff-level route/guard/trainId changes and covering-test deletion are not currently observable facts.
finding: needs_new_observer; applicability depends on output from the bun_interlocking_coverage detector.
task_has_acceptance: llm_judged; paths and tokens cannot determine whether a test genuinely drives guard-true inputs through production resolution and execution or still proves a changed route.

review.summary: I agree with the auditor's PASS: the sampled, compressed, and shared segments preserve the substantive detector, behavioral-proof, exception, and strict-blocking knowledge. The test procedure is largely actionable, but coder-facing discovery and comment-masking details could be clearer, and activation is not purely Datalog-deterministic because it honestly declares new observers and semantic review judgment.
